Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Need guidance on overrun handling for launch week

Hi Connor,

Quick one — we're planning a marketing-driven launch next month and expect a concentrated spike that will exceed our monthly quota for a short window. Legal asked us to get a clear picture on what happens if we go over: how overrun charges would be billed, whether there's a temporary SKU or rate we can purchase for the week, and if there's any playbook for graceful scaling (so our app doesn't get throttled mid-launch).

Can you share the options and any standard docs? We may need procurement to pre-approve a short-term uplift if the numbers are reasonable.

Thanks,
Jenny Park
Growth Ops — Acme Retail
(jenny@acme-retail.com)

Hi Jenny — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the launch plans. Short answer: yes, we have a few paths. I attached our Overrun Mitigation Playbook (PDF) and a SKU/pricing matrix; I also included a draft SOW template if you need a scoped temporary uplift. High-level options: 

- Short-term uplift SKU (prepay for a 7-day uplift at a blended rate) — fastest to enable from our side.
- Temporary higher-rate on-demand (pay-as-you-go) with a soft true-up mechanism to smooth invoice spikes.
- Hybrid: reserve a modest burst bucket + on-demand for overflow; we can apply a credit if billed over a committed buffer.

Ben — can you confirm the blended week SKU price for Acme (we discussed a pilot rate last quarter)? Laura — flagging any contractual or PO timing considerations we should surface to Jenny/procurement.

Jenny — if you can tell us estimated peak TPS and expected total tokens/day for the 7-day window, we can give a tighter number and a PO template.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Proposed commercial response for Acme uplift

Connor / Laura — quick internal note on what I recommend we offer: 

- For a one-week uplift SKU: offer the prepay 7-day SKU at our standard uplift rate but with a one-time promotional discount of 12% for Acme (conditional on signing the 3-month bridge that converts 50% of uplift consumption to a short-term commit). This keeps predictable economics for Acme and reduces our billing churn.
- Invoice timing: we can invoice up front for the 7-day SKU (PO-friendly). Post-usage overrun true-ups (if any) would be invoiced in the next billing cycle; we can provide a single consolidated invoice if Acme prefers.
- Legal addendum: Laura — propose a short addendum (SOW annex) that references the temporary SKU, start/end dates, and a cap for emergency auto-rollbacks. I attached a draft SOW for reference.

Risks/notes: the promotional discount is limited to launches during Q1 and requires finance sign-off; we should cap total promotional exposure to avoid open-ended credits.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Growth — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(Attachment: draft-sow-acme.docx)

Jenny / Tom — thanks for the details. Based on your expected traffic profile (as discussed) and internal approval, here's what we can offer for the launch window: 

1) 7-day uplift SKU (prepay): we will issue an invoice up front for the uplift SKU so Acme can route a single PO through AP. The SKU price is the blended uplift rate; we're applying a one-time 12% promotional discount (max promo credit $25,000) conditional on a 3-month bridge agreement that converts 50% of uplift consumption into a short-term commit.

2) Invoice/true-up flow: any usage beyond the prepay SKU during the window will be captured as a post-usage true-up and invoiced in the next billing cycle. We will provide a consolidated invoice option — uplifts + true-up in one PDF — to simplify AP.

3) Contracting: Laura will send a short addendum (SOW annex) that states the uplift start/end dates, billing flow, and promo cap. That will be sufficient; no full contract amendment required.

If that works, Tom — can you confirm whether we should send the invoice now for PO approval or wait until we receive the final estimated token numbers? If you prefer to lock PO before the launch window, we can push the invoice immediately.

I'll attach the playbook and the SKU/pricing matrix again for reference.

Best,
